title: legal redlines scratchpad - partner agreement v2
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for redlining Partner Agreement v2 (hosted API + dedicated options). Informal notes / negotiation playbook.

Top-level items to watch / flags:
- Data use / training: customer insists on "no use for model training" for hosted API unless explicit opt-in. Need a clear opt-out clause and telemetry privacy carve-outs. For Dedicated/Private, ensure clause states vendor will not use customer data for model improvements.
- Confidential info scope: define that customer prompts, inputs, and outputs are Customer Confidential Information. Avoid broad definitions that allow vendor to reuse outputs.
- Ownership of outputs: push language that customer owns outputs and derivative works produced from their data; vendor retains model IP and improvements.
- Liability cap: propose cap = greater of (fees paid in prior 12 months) and $1M. Customer will ask for higher; consider tiered cap for enterprise (negotiate to fees x12 or flat $5M if strategic).
- Carve-outs to liability cap: include gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP indemnity carve-outs.
- Indemnity: vendor indemnifies for third-party IP infringement of the running service; customer indemnifies for misuse (e.g., illegal requests). Consider mutual indemnity language but keep IP indemnity vendor-forward.
- Data breach / security incident: require notification within 72 hours, root cause analysis, remediation plan, reasonable costs of notification. For regulated customers, expect additional audit rights.
- Audit rights: restrict vendor/customer audit rights to 1x/year, limited scope, and require NDA for auditors. Consider cost-shift back to requesting party unless critical.
- SLA & remedies: customer will push for termination right after repeated SLA misses. Prefer service credits curve (eg. 10% monthly credit per major breach, capped) and a 30-day cure period before termination. Define scheduled maintenance windows and emergency maintenance carve-outs.
- Subprocessors / subcontractors: require list and prior notice for new subprocessors that handle customer data; add right to object. For Private deployments, minimize subprocessor footprint.
- Encryption & keys: BYOK for enterprise / private customers. For hosted API, offer optional KMS integration and contractual guarantees (no key export).
- Logs & retention: define retention windows and deletion obligations on termination. Customer wants guaranteed deletion of customer data within X days; propose 90 days standard, 30 days for sensitive regulated customers with add-on.
- Export controls / compliance: ensure indemnity/assistance for export investigations. Confirm vendor will comply and notify if any restrictions impact service.
- Regulatory obligations & data residency: include commitments for data residency when required (EU/UK), and SOC2 / ISO statements. For healthcare/PHI, need BAAs and HIPAA language.
- Model safety / misuse clause: add prohibited uses (illegal activity, bio/chem misuse). Include escalation process for content takedown.
- Transition assistance: require 60 days of assistance on termination for export of data, keys, and final logs; define format and costs (reasonable, capped).

Negotiation talking points / playbook:
- If customer pushes training prohibition on hosted API, offer explicit product feature ("no training") for an operational fee or as part of enterprise plan.
- On liability cap: move from unlimited to fees*12 + carve-outs. If customer insists on higher, trade off for higher fees or stricter security controls / audits.
- SLA: offer service credits and 30-day cure before termination. Keep termination only for repeated missed SLOs or material breach.
- Data deletion: commit to deletion within 90 days by default. For stricter customers, offer 30-day deletion + audit trail as paid add-on.
- Audit frequency: cap to 1x/year, on-site requires 30 days notice, remote preferred.
- IP indemnity: accept on vendor-owned model and infra; exclude claims arising from customer-provided prompts or combined use with third-party models.

Redline snippets to propose (informal):
- Data use: "Vendor will not use Customer Data (including prompts and outputs) to train or improve models used in the Service, except with Customer's prior written consent."
- Liability: "Except for breaches of confidentiality, willful misconduct, or gross negligence, each party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (a) fees paid by Customer to Vendor under this Agreement in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000."
- SLA termination: "Customer may terminate for material repeated breaches of the SLA only if Vendor fails to remedy the breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice specifying the breach."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm what product-level "no training" option looks like (engineering + pricing). Loop in Product (Maya) for implementation note.
- Security team (Jordan) to confirm acceptable audit process and frequency.
- Commercial: if customer asks for higher liability cap, what pricing uplift grid do we present? (FYI: sales guidelines needed)
- Does Dedicated contract default to same data-use language? Likely must strengthen to no training.

Contextual notes / references:
- Customer: mid-market fintech, strict compliance needs (SaaS with PII + transaction data). Likely to request BAA and SOC2 Type II.
- Related artifacts: see Confluence page CONFLUENCE-legal/partner-agreement-v2 for full draft; JIRA-RED-3342 tracks commercial terms.

Quick negotiation play: prioritize Data-use + SLA + Liability in that order. If forced to trade, consider narrower SLA credits (not termination) and monetize "no training" as premium feature.

Notes to self (shorthand):
- push for mutual confidentiality, customer owns outputs, vendor retains model IP, no training without consent, liability cap = fees*12 or 1M, carve-outs for gross negligence + IP.
- security notify 72h, audit 1x/year, BYOK for ent.
- retention 90d default, 30d add-on.

Next steps:
- Draft proposed redlines using the 3 bullets above and circulate to Maya/Jordan for signoff.
- Prepare 1-pager for Sales to explain tradeoffs (pricing for no-training + liability increases).
- Add a short fallback clause if customer insists on lower cap: require higher fees + escalation to legal SVP.

End of scratchpad.
